PersonaFactoryStylistic User Prompt Augmentation with Synthetic Persona Bank

Bich Ngoc Doan1, Hanna Yukhymenko2, Imanol Schlag2

1EPFL   2ETH Zurich

Paper (soon) Code Dataset

Abstract.Large language models increasingly replace real people in the AI development pipeline, as they are used to generate training dialogues at scale, control alignment and evaluation. However, out-of-the-box models produce monolingual and stylistically flat texts as synthetic user prompts, failing to replicate the real user-AI communication mechanics. We present PersonaFactory, an end-to-end pipeline to generate detailed user personas, later using them to augment existing user prompts from their point of view. As part of this work, we showcase two major data contributions, facilitating research in LLM-based stylistic chat generation. First, we release a bank of over 740,000 structured, fully synthetic personas, focusing on their background and communication behavior with a chatbot. Second, we release a corpus of roughly 1.24 million persona-styled synthetic conversations spanning 85 languages, produced by using the generated bank of personas to augment existing user prompts and match personas to them based on original prompt intent and profile background. We also provide an ablation study of the assistant persona design for response augmentation and downstream performance after training on such conversations. Finally, we evaluate the effect of personal features on style adoption and intent preservation, using an LLM-judge and heuristic metrics to assess augmentation efficiency. We find that simulating users' unique behavioral features in the conversation greatly benefits from a structured, attribute-based approach, compared to a single free-text description in existing personalization methods. We show that the produced augmented data is hard to distinguish from human-written texts for real people and that PersonaFactory as a training artifact can improve model adaptive behavior purely from data impact without steering.

  • 743,010structured synthetic personas
  • 1.24Mpersona-styled conversations
  • 85languages in the corpus

Findings

Finding 1

Structured style beats a free-text description

60% vs 33% preferred

Rewriter, persona and length budget are held fixed. The judge prefers the rewrite with per-axis style keys nearly twice as often as the free-text one. Intent preservation is 92% for both, and the three external judges agree.

Finding 2

Rewrites read as human-written

59% judged human by raters

Raters who work in AI took 59% of verified rewrites for human-written and told rewrites from real messages apart with 55% accuracy. LLM judges took 83–89% of them for human-written and did no better than chance at telling the two apart.

Finding 3

Training on it makes models adapt to the user

0.18 → 0.51 formality tracking

After fine-tuning on persona-styled chats, Llama-3.1-8B follows the user's formality and emoji use much more closely than the instruct release. The judge prefers its replies 79% of the time, or 69% when reply length is controlled.

From persona to conversation

We start from a real chat log. A matched persona re-voices each user turn, and the request and its constraints stay the same. The assistant turns are then regenerated, and a judge screens the whole conversation. Pick a conversation from the released dataset and run it through the line.

Numbered marks link a span of the rewrite to the profile field it comes from. Hover either side.
R1 · keep the taskConservative matching

Language and script are detected first. The persona must be a native speaker of the prompt's language. Among those, the match comes from location, then top-1 embedding similarity, then the language pool. If nothing matches, the turn is kept verbatim.

R2 · diversify registerConstrained rewrite

Quotes, code, URLs and numbers are masked and restored. Quirks fire with p = 0.25 per turn so that personas do not turn into caricatures. Rewrites shorter than 50% of the original are rejected.

R3 · stay on trajectoryContinuity supervision

The real next user message serves as weak supervision. A judge checks that the regenerated reply still leads to it, and the reply is adapted for up to two rounds.

R4 · no hidden shortcutSix-class sanity gate

Language mismatch, format violation, truncation, fabricated experience, hallucination, unaddressed request. Only the conversation turns are stored. The persona is not.

Quality control

We check each rewrite for two things: whether it still asks for the same thing (intent) and whether it sounds like the persona (style). Model judges and plain string checks test both in several ways, and the QC sheet collects the results. In the last stage, people rate samples in languages they know well.

Left: what is inspected and how. Right: the result. Hover a mark for exact values.

Tuning the machine

The rewriting step has five settings. The paper changes one at a time and holds the rest fixed. Pick a setting to see what was measured.

Rewriter versus attribute Table 22 · Fig. 25 read from figure

On a shared axis, the eight attribute families sit close together while the four rewriters spread out.

Family means Table 22

Each family averages its two conditions over four rewriters. Every family scores 0.06 to 0.07 below the no-persona baseline on script stability.

Assistant line and training bay

With varied users alone, a model still answers everyone in one default style. The release therefore matches each conversation to one of 12 assistant response styles and regenerates the replies in that style. An ablation then trains Llama-3.1-8B and Apertus-8B on three versions of the corpus.

Other persona datasets and how to extend them

PersonaHub describes a person in one or two sentences. SynthPAI adds a paragraph on writing style. PersonaFactory keeps a separate style layer with per-axis typing keys. This station compares the formats, then converts Nemotron-Personas and PersonaHub records into PersonaFactory backgrounds and adds a style layer. A further step restyles conversation data that has no user persona.

Six steps, from the existing datasets to a version with a style layer.

Release & citation

The persona bank, the augmented corpus and the pipeline code will be released under a permissive license that explicitly disallows profiling, targeting, and presenting synthetic output as a real person's voice.
